text: Today, we are uncovering the swing trading strategy of a 23-year-old from Hong Kong, who reportedly clocked a 1,358% return in the 2025 US investing championship, and a prior 283% gain in 2024. This is the methodical breakdown of Martin Luke's systematic approach that transformed him from buying GameStop at the exact parabolic high in 2021 to becoming a top performer in the most prestigious trading competition in the world. From tripling his account with beginner's luck to seeing a 50% drawdown to becoming a winner of the USIC, Martin-Luc Castinator will dissect every component of his trading system from his pre-market scanning routine to his precise entry techniques, risk management protocols and exit strategies. Will examine his complete methodology. the three scanner system that identifies opportunities, the entry techniques that minimize risk, the position sizing that maximizes geometric growth, and the exit strategies that capture trends whilst protecting capital. What makes Luke's story particularly valuable is his transparency about mistakes. Even whilst achieving triple digit returns, he violated his own rules multiple times, demonstrating that trading can be forgiving if your risk management is on point. Good trading is always about disciplined maintenance of an edge through systematic execution. Let's start with a foundation. Martin's risk-first philosophy. Martin Luke's entire system revolves around a fundamental principle. I can't predict the return of my trade, but I can limit my risk. This philosophy manifests in his core statistics from 2024. 104 winners against 319 losers. building a 23% win rate. His average winner generated 15% returns, whilst average losses were contained to 3%. The mathematical edge lies in this risk-reward asymmetry. When you risk 3% to make 15%, you only need to be right 17% of the time to break even. But Luke's edge extends beyond simple mathematics. This tight stop loss strategy creates what he calls a parabolic relationship between stop widths and risk multiples. When he tightens a stop from 3% to 1.5% on a 25% winning trade, he gains an additional 8 risk multiple. On a 50% winner, that same tightening adds 17 risk multiples. This exponential benefit explains why precision in entries becomes paramount. Let's now look at Martin's the three scanner discovery system. Martin has a standard criterion for all stocks. He's chasing fast-moving stocks in hot sectors which generally have an average daily range or ADR of over 5%. Luke's opportunity identification relies on three distinct scanners, each serving a specific purpose in his systematic approach. Firstly, the pre-market scanner. This filters stocks gapping higher on significant volume. This pre-market routine identifies momentum before the market opens, allowing him to prepare for potential episodic pivot opportunities. This scanner is the same as the one Christian Kalamagi uses to find stocks that are gapping up, and I'll leave a link to his video at the end. Next, the potent scanner reveals the previous day's strongest performers, helping identify sector rotation and thematic momentum. When multiple stocks from the same sector appear consistently, it signals money flow that often continues into subsequent sessions. This is how he caught the quantum computing theme and cryptocurrency-related momentum that drove Manny off his largest winners. Then, the leader scanner provides a weekly perspective, ranking stocks by monthly performance to identify sustained relative strengths. In strong markets, this list expands significantly. During corrections, it contracts dramatically, serving as a market health indicator that influences his overall positioning. These scanners don't just find stocks, they provide market context that influences position sizing, holding periods and exit strategies. A simple observation of the number of stocks in these scans can tell you the strength or the weakness in the market. Once he has the watchlist, Martin would shortlist the best actionable names based on their price action. The idea is to focus on the names that are taking support from or reclaiming key moving averages, specifically the 9, 21 and 50 EMA in a base, or focus on the best movers in the pre-market session. Let's now come to precision entry techniques. Martin's entry methodology centres on range expansion from tight consolidations, but with crucial refinements that separate his approach from traditional breakout trading. Prior day high breakouts represent his primary setup. However, he doesn't simply buy breakouts, he waits for specific conditions. The ideal scenario involves an inside day or extremely tight range, followed by a gap up that opens in the upper portion of the previous day's range, and then breaks the prior day's high. This entry is best executed when the price converges with major EMAs, the 9, 21 and 50, whilst forming an inside candle or a tight area. Opening range highs provide intraday precision to enter episodic pivots. Using one minute chart immediately after the open, or five minute chart once that timeframe establishes, he enters when stocks break above the opening range high. The stop sits at the opening range low, creating clearly defined risk parameters. Intraday range highs offer re-entry opportunities when initial breakouts fail. If a stock fails at the opening range high but maintains bullish characteristics, he He seeks secondary breakout levels using five-minute consolidations above the nine EMA. The critical insight from his analysis reveals why precision matters. Traditional breakout entries might require six to seven percent stops, making position sizing problematic. His refined entries often allow two to three percent stops, enabling larger position sizes, whilst maintaining identical dollar risk. He frequently shuffles between daily, hourly and five-minute charts to spot the best lowest risk entry points. Let's understand position sizing and risk management from Martin Luke's perspective. He risks 0.5% of his portfolio per trade, but this baseline adjusts based on market conditions and personal performance. During drawdowns, he reduces position size to test the waters. With profit cushions and favorable markets, he then increases exposure. Maximum portfolio exposure reaches 35% for large-cap liquid stocks, reducing to 25% to 30% for small and micro-caps due to gap-down risk. His stop-loss methodology prioritises the low of the breakout day, based on extensive chart study showing that genuine breakouts rarely revisit their breakout lows. In the distance between entry and day low exceeds 5%, he uses the 5-minute entry candle low instead. Let's now understand Martin's exit strategy framework. Martin employs both strength-based and weakness-based exits, with selection depending on market stage, position profitability and overall portfolio context. Selling into strength occurs in 10-15% increments when profits exceed three risk multiples, position size grows beyond 35% due to appreciation, stocks become extended from the 9 EMA, he feels euphoric about the position. Selling into weakness utilizes trailing stops primarily the 9 EMA for most positions. With strong uptrends with early entries, he'll use the 21 or even 50 EMA to avoid premature exits. The key insight. Exit strategy adapts to market stage and equity curve position. During drawdowns, he leans towards selling in strength to preserve capital. With profit cushions and strong markets, he trails positions longer to capture extended moves. Let's now look at a case study from Martin's trade in 2024, the GameStop trade. Martin's May 2024 GameStop trade exemplifies his evolved methodology. Entering at $26.30 with a stop at $25.47, he captured a 40-risk multiple return as the stock exploded to over $50. The entry came on the opening-range breakout in this gap-up on a one-minute timeframe, the stop set at the prior minute bar low rather than the days low. This was an episodic pivot trade that violated his typical day-low stop rule, but the day-low would have required over 6% risk, unacceptable for his system, so he adapted in this trade to manage the risk. For exit, he trimmed half the position at 12 risk multiples. Near $37, a 37% move. The remainder he held
